title: App Health
description: Single-pane health view: alerts, per-namespace app health, nodes, NFS storage and the monitoring stack itself.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Firing alerts excluding the always-on Watchdog and InfoInhibitor.

panels.title: Unhealthy pods
panels.description: Pods Pending/Failed/Unknown plus containers stuck waiting (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ...).

targets.expr: (count(kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Pending|Failed|Unknown", namespace=~"$namespace"} == 1) or vector(0)) + (count(kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{reason!="ContainerCreating", namespace=~"$namespace"} == 1) or vector(0))

panels.title: Hottest Pi
panels.description: Pi 4 SoC throttles from ~80 C.

panels.title: Fullest node filesystem
panels.description: Worst of / and /mnt/* across nodes. /mnt/ssd on the NFS node backs every PVC.

panels.title: /mnt/ssd time to full
panels.description: Linear projection from the last 6h. Very large when the share is not filling.

panels.title: Prometheus head span
panels.description: Healthy is <= 3h. Anything above means the head cannot compact and prometheus is rewriting its WAL in a loop (what saturated wk-03 -> wk-01 NFS).

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Everything currently firing except Watchdog/InfoInhibitor. Click an alertname in Alertmanager for the runbook.

panels.title: Namespace health
panels.description: One line per namespace. Network for hostNetwork pods (cilium, node-exporter, metallb speaker) mirrors the node NIC, so kube-system/monitoring/metallb-system read high by design.

panels.title: Pods not healthy
panels.description: Containers stuck in a waiting state and pods not Running/Succeeded.

panels.title: Restarts per pod (1h)
panels.description: Only pods that restarted in the last hour.

panels.title: Memory: working set vs limit (top 10)
panels.description: Containers closest to being OOM-killed. Only containers with a memory limit appear.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (namespace, pod, container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{container!="", container!="POD", namespace=~"$namespace"}) / sum by (namespace, pod, container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{resource="memory", namespace=~"$namespace"}) * 100)

panels.title: CPU throttling (top 10, 5m)
panels.description: Share of CFS periods in which the container hit its CPU limit. Sustained >25% means the limit is too low.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (namespace, pod, container) (increase(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{container!="", namespace=~"$namespace"}[5m])) / sum by (namespace, pod, container) (increase(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{container!="", namespace=~"$namespace"}[5m])) * 100 > 0)

panels.title: Network per pod (top 10)
panels.description: RX+TX. hostNetwork pods report the whole node NIC.

panels.title: Workloads with unavailable replicas
panels.description: Empty is good.

panels.title: Network transmit
panels.description: Physical NIC only. On this cluster all PVC I/O is NFS to a worker node, so a sustained high line here is usually storage traffic.

panels.title: Load (1m) per core
panels.description: >1 means runnable work is queuing.

panels.title: NFS client writes per node
panels.description: Which node is writing to the NFS share. A node stuck at tens of ops/s is a pod rewriting its volume in a loop.

panels.title: NFS server ops
panels.description: Served by the node exporting /mnt/ssd.

panels.title: PVC usage
panels.description: NFS PVCs have no quota, so every claim reports the usage of the whole share; a jump here means the share itself is filling.

panels.title: Prometheus head span
panels.description: Should sit between 1h and 3h.

panels.title: Compactions per hour
panels.description: Normal is about 1 every 2h. The NFS write storm was ~100/h.

panels.title: Scrape targets down by job
panels.description: Empty is good.
